rules: The National Polygon Dataset is HM Land Registry's published Index Polygons dataset, while INSPIRE Index Polygons is a subset of the wider Index Polygons database.
HM Land Registry states that title plans and registers normally record the general position of boundaries unless an exact boundary has been determined.
Each registered title is represented in the Index Map by at least one index polygon.
A title plan and its register share the same title number, while the corresponding index polygon carries its own unique Poly_ID.
An index polygon is an index to the location of a registered title and does not by itself define the exact legal extent of ownership.
An index polygon may be the same size as, larger than, or smaller than the extent shown on the title plan.
HM Land Registry maps index polygons against Ordnance Survey large-scale mapping where the ownership boundary follows a mapped physical feature.
HM Land Registry notes that ownership boundaries do not always follow features shown on Ordnance Survey mapping.
HM Land Registry receives Ordnance Survey MasterMap change-only updates for ongoing mapping work.
Ordnance Survey MasterMap change-only updates are not used as a routine process to retrospectively reposition every existing registration.
HM Land Registry's polygon data has a history of vectorisation from earlier paper and raster map records.
HM Land Registry describes a Polygon Accuracy Improvement programme that adjusted polygon geometry against improved Ordnance Survey mapping.
HM Land Registry describes a later Quality Improvement Framework programme that reconciled many index polygons against title-plan evidence.
HM Land Registry records urban, semi-rural and mountain/moorland Ordnance Survey capture scales of 1:1250, 1:2500 and 1:10000 respectively.
HM Land Registry states that its spatial data and index polygons are captured in British National Grid coordinates.
Publication validation checks include detection of polygons containing zero coordinate values.
Publication validation checks include detection of zero-area polygons.
Publication validation checks include duplicate coordinate points within polygon geometry.
HM Land Registry reports cleanup of many self-intersecting polygon geometries before publication.
Polygons smaller than 0.1 square metres are removed from the published National Polygon Dataset.
The Planning Data entity search endpoint uses /entity.{extension}, where the documented extensions are json, html and geojson.
The q parameter is documented for postcode or UPRN search.
The typology parameter can filter entity search by typology.
The dataset parameter can filter entity search by dataset.
The organisation_entity parameter can filter entity search by the managing organisation entity.
The entity parameter can filter entity search by entity number.
The curie parameter can filter entity search by CURIE.
The prefix parameter can filter entity search by prefix.
The reference parameter can filter entity search by reference.
The period parameter can restrict entity search to current or all entries.
The start_date_year parameter is documented with start_date_match for start-date filtering.
The start_date_month parameter is documented with start_date_match for start-date filtering.
The start_date_day parameter is documented with start_date_match for start-date filtering.
The end_date_year parameter is documented with end_date_match for end-date filtering.
The end_date_month parameter is documented with end_date_match for end-date filtering.
The end_date_day parameter is documented with end_date_match for end-date filtering.
The entry_date_year parameter is documented with entry_date_match for entry-date filtering.
The quality parameter is available as an entity-search filter.
The field and exclude_field parameters control fields returned by Planning Data API responses.
Planning Data publishes an OpenAPI document at /openapi.json for the current beta API.
The Environment Agency exposes an OGC API - Features landing endpoint for survey index files at /spatialdata/survey-index-files/ogc/features/v1.
The survey-index OGC API landing page identifies the service as part of the Defra Network feature service.
The OGC API collections list includes a collection named LIDAR_Composite_1m_DTM_2022_extents.
The LIDAR_Composite_1m_DTM_2022_extents collection declares storage coordinates in EPSG:27700.
The LIDAR_Composite_1m_DTM_2022_extents collection publishes a geographic bounding extent covering England.
The collection queryables include a filename field.
The collection queryables include a tilename field.
The collection queryables include a polygon_id field.
The collection queryables include a resolution field.
The collection queryables include a year field.
The collection queryables include an od_dtm_fn field.
The collection queryables include an sd_flown field for survey start-date information.
The collection queryables include an ed_flown field for survey end-date information.
The collection queryables include a gdb_geomattr_data field.
The collection schema includes the feature geometry or shape field.
The collection advertises GeoJSON as an available feature representation.
The collection advertises GML 3.2 as an available feature representation.
The collection advertises CSV as an available feature representation.
Official sample feature records expose source-resolution values including 0.25 m, 0.5 m and 1.0 m.
Official sample feature records expose survey start/end dates and source DTM filename fields that can be used for survey provenance.
Ordnance Survey's OpenData automation guide demonstrates discovery through the /downloads/v1/products endpoint without requiring a Premium API key.
OpenData product-list JSON entries include a product Name field.
OpenData product-list JSON entries include a product Description field.
OpenData product-list JSON entries include a Version field.
OpenData product-list JSON entries include a product URL field.
OpenData product-list JSON entries include a product ID field.
Ordnance Survey documents storing and comparing the product Version value to detect later OpenData releases.
Product-specific metadata and download discovery use the product ID obtained from the OpenData product list.
OpenData download lists can contain separate files or packages by area and format.
After selecting a matching OpenData download entry, the documented workflow follows its supplied download URL.
OS Terrain 50 grid data is supplied in ASCII Grid format.
OS Terrain 50 grid delivery includes supporting GML metadata.
The supporting Terrain 50 GML describes grid location, grid spacing and vertical-reference information.
ASCII grid rows contain values ordered from west to east.
Each Terrain 50 ASCII grid row contains 200 pixel values.
The Terrain 50 ASCII grid cell size is 50 metres.
Terrain 50 grid height values are supplied to the nearest 0.1 metre.
A Terrain 50 grid tile supply includes .asc, .gml, .prj, .asc.aux.xml and per-tile Metadata XML files.
Terrain 50 grid tiles do not overlap and do not carry shared common-edge pixel values.
Ordnance Survey warns that small steps can occur at tile edges in tidal-water areas because neighbouring tiles can use different tidal levels.
